name: Octave Duclos
headline: Renewable energy analytics. Smarter decisions.
intro: I turn complex energy data into clear procurement decisions, reliable portfolio insights, and practical tools. My work connects renewable energy economics with AI and automation to help teams move faster and make better decisions.
about: I’m a Senior Analyst in Climate & Sustainability at ERM Coho, with an MSc in Environmental Engineering and a background in physics, philosophy, and quantitative research. I build models, investigate data, and automate recurring work across renewable energy procurement and portfolio management.

projects.title: A common framework for VPPA decisions
projects.summary: Advancing a firm-wide model for comparing renewable energy opportunities across the U.S. and Canada.
projects.context: Renewable energy bids differ in market exposure, contract structure, and environmental impact. Comparing them requires a consistent view of economics and assumptions.
projects.work: Own and advance an Excel/VBA model integrating developer bids, wholesale prices, contract terms, and emissions factors. Evaluate project economics across scenarios and maintain version control in GitHub.
projects.result: A business-critical analytical foundation for procurement recommendations and market intelligence.

projects.title: From settlements to portfolio insight
projects.summary: Turning operating PPA data into forecasts, reconciled reporting, and answers clients can use.
projects.context: Operating renewable energy portfolios require recurring oversight of generation, availability, settlements, and financial performance.
projects.work: Manage reporting across 13+ operating projects for 3+ clients. Prepare portfolio forecasts using forward prices, settlement structures, generation forecasts, and technology assumptions; audit invoices and availability reports and work with developers and meter agents to investigate discrepancies.
projects.result: Produced 70+ portfolio forecasts and audited 200+ invoices and reports, supporting financial reporting and ongoing portfolio oversight.

projects.title: Less manual work. More time for analysis.
projects.summary: Using AI and workflow automation to accelerate recurring energy reporting.
projects.context: Energy reporting often starts with complex invoices and settlement documents that need to be translated into consistent reporting formats.
projects.work: Build workflows using AI, Python, and Power Automate to extract invoice information and prepare settlement summaries and performance reports.
projects.result: Generated 50+ summaries and reports through automated workflows, streamlining recurring report preparation.

projects.title: Finding the value of community solar
projects.summary: A portfolio model connecting hourly generation, utility rules, and REC strategy.
projects.context: The value of a new solar project depends on its interaction with existing contracts, electricity demand, credit banking, and utility program rules.
projects.work: Built a model combining client load, 8,760-hour generation profiles, existing renewable contracts, REC markets, and virtual net metering rules. Modeled monthly matching, annual credit banking, nonlinear credit tiers, and alternative procurement scenarios.
projects.result: Supported project selection and contracting for a 25-year solar project delivering approximately 28,000 MWh per year, and identified an approximately $2M annual REC arbitrage opportunity over 10 years.

images.alt: Portfolio forecast comparing client electricity load, existing renewable generation, and proposed community solar generation over time.
images.caption: Portfolio load and generation forecast, including contract expirations, REC needs, and community solar scenarios. Original portfolio excerpt; assumptions reflect the project at the time.

projects.title: A practical path to lower emissions
projects.summary: Translating fragmented enterprise data into a renewable energy procurement strategy.
projects.context: A decentralized aeronautics company with 100+ global business units needed a Scope 1 and 2 baseline and a pathway to a 50% emissions reduction by 2031.
projects.work: Cleaned and reconciled utility and load data and modeled onsite solar, utility green tariffs, retail renewable electricity, and portfolio-level VPPA procurement.
projects.result: Determined that a single U.S. VPPA could cover North American Scope 2 emissions and achieve the modeled 2031 target.

projects.title: Making automation useful across a team
projects.summary: Building reusable workflows and helping colleagues put AI into everyday practice.
projects.context: Scaling automation takes both useful tools and the confidence to apply them to real work.
projects.work: Lead Python/API automation for market, policy, and client intelligence; standardize reusable codebases; deliver AI training and office hours as part of the Coho AI Team. Automate project resourcing forecasts by integrating Salesforce data with existing planning templates.
projects.result: Expanded access to practical AI and automation through shared tools, training, and ongoing support. An internal research agent remained in use more than 1.5 years after creation.
